title: Building a Portfolio with 5 ETFs
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
summary: On Mark Roussin's own channel, he and guest Joseph Hogue assemble a five-ETF 'foundation' portfolio. The picks: VOO (Mark's; the no-brainer backbone - his first dollars invested, still adding); CIBR, the First Trust cybersecurity ETF (Joseph's pick; Mark enthusiastically endorses it - cybersecurity is the one tech-budget line item that can't be cut, ~12%/yr spend growth; holds CRWD, PANW, FTNT, ZS); SCHD (Mark's; 'far and away the best dividend ETF,' 3.5% yield, ~10% five-year dividend growth, 14 straight years of growth; top sectors now staples/healthcare/energy); AIQ, the AI & technology ETF (Joseph's pick; 84 names from NVDA/AMD/ASML/TSM to NFLX/AAPL; Mark calls it a 'fantastic addition' and singles out his love for Taiwan Semi); and IJR, iShares Core S&P Small-Cap (Mark's; quality small caps over IWM's broad basket, 656 holdings, 0.06% expense ratio). Joseph's model allocation: 25% VOO / 20% SCHD / 30% AIQ / 20% CIBR / 5% IJR. Mark's: 30% VOO / ~30% SCHD / 25% AIQ / 10% CIBR / 5% IJR, tuned to risk tolerance and IJR underweight while rates stay high. Education-first: balance, position sizing, complementing growth with income. Calls: VOO, SCHD, CIBR, AIQ, IJR all BUY (Mark); TSM UNCERTAIN (passing mention). Note: component names CRWD/PANW/FTNT/ZS are CIBR holdings, not individual calls.
